summary.text: A 35-year-old woman presented with pain on chewing and swelling on the right side of the face. Examination found a grossly carious, tender right mandibular first molar and an extensive multilocular radiolucency of the mandible. She was diagnosed with right buccal and submandibular space infection and a panmandibular cystic lesion, provisionally OKC. Incisional biopsy confirmed nonsyndromic parakeratinized odontogenic keratocyst.

The infections were treated surgically and the offending tooth was extracted. Marsupialization was done with bone windows, socket enlargement, evacuation and povidone-iodine packing, followed by periodic irrigation. Immunohistochemistry of the pretreatment biopsy showed abundant Ki-67 and bcl-2, which were reduced at the base of the resolved lesion. Radiographs at 4 months showed gradual resolution except a small area in the mandibular right quadrant.

After 2 years radiolucency persisted with root divergence in the 42 and 43 region, which was curetted out with Carnoy's solution cauterization. After 6 months without resolution, the labial cortex and associated teeth were removed with repeat Carnoy's cauterization. Loss of labial vestibule followed and prosthetic rehabilitation was done. Follow-up for up to 10 years showed total uneventful bone healing with no recurrence or new lesion.
